claim: Complete opt data/notification/constructor package. Existing native default initialization and region scan callers migrate; no PD root, discovery, TSO, grpcutil or transport package acceptance.

package_artifacts.integration: src/pd/opt.rs: every source type, static field, dynamic setting/channel, constructor and option builder; declaration_mapping and dependency_decisions describe native representations.

src/pd/opt_tests.rs: original TestDynamicOptionChange/TestOptions and deterministic equivalents of clearChannel/ensureNoNotification; race/goleak on original Go. Additional full-constructor/shared-identity/channel/concurrency coverage.

type_mapping.Option: Options, typed atomic fields instead of heterogeneous atomic.Value array
type_mapping.GetRegionOp: GetRegionOp; RegionScanOptions is a compatibility type alias only

dependency_decisions.native: std::time::Duration admits nonnegative durations only; negative Go duration states are not expressible. Concurrency and retry count retain signed machine width with isize/AtomicIsize and no validation. Metadata signed fields stay i64. Interval validation covers inclusive 0..10ms with exact nanoseconds.

Typed sequentially consistent atomics preserve the source single-CAS behavior, including successful setter return after losing an interval CAS. Capacity-one Tokio channels coalesce changes and retain pending data across canceled receives. Receiver mutex is the language adapter for one owned Tokio receiver, not a worker or polling loop. Sending a real change after caller closure panics like Go. Options is constructed before Arc sharing instead of copying synchronization primitives.

Opaque append-ordered Arc<Fn(Endpoint)->Endpoint> handles. This package only stores options; complete grpcutil dialing, interceptors/reconnection and execution of those options remain parent/dependency work, not accepted here.

Optional Arc<RwLock<HashMap>> retains mutable label-map identity; existing SharedBackoffer retains policy identity. RangeEnd is a fixed Arc<[AtomicU8]> so shared byte updates remain visible without changing slice length or introducing data races. Option closures retain those handles across repeated application; None represents nil.

Reusable Send+Sync boxed Fn closures, applied in source order; append dial options, replace scalar/shared values, preserve unrelated request fields. NewOption maps to Options::new/default. Native export pd_options owns the API; pd_backoff exposes the already-implemented input policy.

Original tests run unmodified with Go race/goleak. Native synchronous setters allow immediate deterministic notification assertions; all spawned test threads join, and no implementation worker is spawned. All five shared support sources remain inventoried including Linux/non-Linux variants.
